task: Audit reproducibility of the existing formal research/publication flow; repair concrete gaps

conclusion.engineering: The standard path already carries real-first discovery, individual fallback review, counterevidence admission and immutable publication. Identified reproducibility/recovery gaps have been repaired in the development checkout.
conclusion.quality: No new independent chapter was generated. Reproducing chapter one's final 99.5% or learner benefit is not established by these contract tests.
conclusion.activation: Not yet copied to the production runtime or main while independent textbook transfer is awaiting the user's VIX-source boundary decision.

findings.issue: Normal VIX input/candidate/mark tools depended on abandoned Seed, memberships, textbook and generator paths.
findings.fix: New input access pins only data/seed-access; legacy inventories remain byte-for-byte but out-of-scope files are never read/fetched. Candidates use index navigation honestly without inventing full memberships. Project-owned marks-only derivation preserves identity and can recover interrupted date-derived writes.

findings.issue: Dictionary retrieval was coupled to the VIX commit and could automatically read/fetch prohibited textbook paths.
findings.fix: Prepared an independently pinned Second Language library with explicit authorized-directory transfer, full hash checks, per-run source locks, plan/material/evidence binding and normal archive inclusion. Actual originals have NOT been transferred pending the scope decision.

findings.issue: Production plan sealed selected IDs and dictionary packets but omitted actual selection reasons and learner feedback.
findings.fix: New plans pin original UTF-8 selection.md and feedback.json. Optional rewritten summaries do not replace them. Existing plans/handwritten historical records are not rewritten.

findings.issue: Lost final return recovery covered initial assembly but missed repaired assembly.
findings.fix: Both assembly paths read and verify the same actual publication before considering another generation. Unconfirmed/unknown invocations remain protected.

findings.issue: One automatic repair round was not persisted across a host restart.
findings.fix: Persist the exact plan and repair digest in automatic-repair.json; restart cannot grant a second round.

findings.issue: A legacy publication fixture asserted obsolete unbound 40-word/audio behavior.
findings.fix: The existing command now executes maintained control, source/evidence and usage-context SQLite/Worker suites, including actual 30-word fixture publication/readback.

findings.issue: Some current prose retained obsolete 50-word and raw-membership requirements.
findings.fix: Align active selection/production instructions to 30 words and allowed index scope, retaining frozen historical contracts.

findings.issue: Scheduler completion records were hard to compare with chapter one's quality outcome.
findings.fix: Successful publication preflight/results now carry recomputed authenticity coverage, admission/alarm and actual approved example IDs; no model-written percentage and no semantic-truth claim.

findings.issue: Missing independent textbook library could be discovered after starting a planning model.
findings.fix: Verify library before any new model invocation; rest and verified-publication recovery need no model.

alreadyClosedAndVerified: 100% real-first discovery with exact original/sense/function witnesses
Independent isolated fallback review with actual records, per-case reuse and negative decisions
Source counterevidence blocks both signers and publisher before credentials/network
Canonical body/source preseal, full permanent GET/SHA and lost-ACK recovery
Native Goal completion verified against real artifacts; no host continue loop or unknown replay
remaining: User decision on retaining the existing full textbooks as an independently sealed Second Language library under the index-only VIX boundary.
If approved: transfer and verify the exact originals, validate real independent lookups and private recovery, then fast-forward the production runtime and push main.
A future normally authorized chapter is required to measure repeatability of source quality, correction effort and total Codex usage; this audit does not trigger one.
